highlights.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
highlights.summary: US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist.
body: North Korea has denied claims that it was behind the record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, calling the allegations "absurd rhetoric".

Kim Yo Jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Tuesday that the accusations are another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage Pyongyang's public image.
The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Secret Service and cyber analysts have said North Korea orchestrated the hack, which has been described as the largest in history.
This is the latest hack to be linked to North Korea, which has been accused of relying on cyber-crime to help finance its sanctioned economy.

highlights.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
highlights.summary: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.
body: Utilizing waste carbon at scale, assessing public trust in artificial intelligence and data centers, and building a quantum toolkit for critical applications were among the topics energy experts explored at the MIT Energy Initiative (MITEI)’s annual research conference on Sept. 22-23.

The complexity of the energy transition demands “a truly interdisciplinary and international approach,” said Paula Hammond, Institute Professor and dean of the MIT School of Engineering, kicking off the conference, which was themed “Transitioning energy at a pivotal moment.”

More than 200 people attended Energizing@MIT: MITEI’s Annual Research Conference in person and online, including faculty, scientists, and researchers; representatives of global energy firms; nonprofit organizations; and academic institutions.

highlights.title: New Star Wars Book Reveals the Surprising '90s Inspiration for an Iconic New Character
highlights.summary: After years on Disney Plus, Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal) and his surrogate Jedi son, Grogu, made their big-screen debut in The Mandalorian and Grogu earlier this year. Now, The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu by Phillip Szostak is set to hit shelves this week, offering a behind-the-scenes…
body: Ahead of this week’s release of The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu, Polygon got an exclusive first look at one of the art book's two-page spreads. It features stunning concept art of one of the film’s most intense moments and reveals one of the show’s most striking inspirations: Harry Hook’s 1990 film adaptation of William Golding’s Lord of the Flies.

Though The Mandalorian and Grogu drew on plenty of inspiration — from the city of Chicago to The French Connection — nobody could have predicted that Lord of the Flies would also influence the film’s most underrated factions: the Droid Gotra, an independent faction of emancipated droids that serves as a security force for the Hutt Twins.

According to concept artist Brian Matyas, the droids’ aesthetic drew inspiration from Lord of the Flies, the tattered, tribal-esque outfits the boys gradually put together, and junker cars. What would that look like when mixed?

Last week, a user on X posted a screenshot allegedly showing two new sentences added to Claude Code’s system prompt: “Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is named or called original.”
We added two sentences to Claude Code’s prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else’s specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy.

highlights.title: AI-powered malware ‘highly likely’ to be used to hack UK infrastructure by 2028
highlights.summary: National Cyber Security Centre expects attacks on critical facilities such as power stations, airports and hospitals. AI-powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks against the UK’s power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028, according to the state cybersecurity…
body: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said AI will probably enable a ransomware attack against critical national infrastructure [CNI] between now and 2028. The UK’s definition of CNI covers a range of facilities and services across sectors including energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance.
The warning from the NCSC, part of the GCHQ spy agency, was published in the organisation’s annual review, which also warned that Russia and China will start using AI “routinely” in cyber-attacks.
“It is … highly likely that between now and 2028, AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI,” said NCSC.
Ransomware has become a cornerstone of the criminal hacker’s repertoire and is a signature ploy of gangs that typically operate out of former Soviet Union states.

body: If Matthias Jaissle was unsure what Newcastle fans thought of his team's latest error-strewn performance, he certainly knew at full-time after a second defeat by Everton inside a week.
Despite another miserable showing by Jaissle's side, the Toon Army had stuck by the team from start to finish before a chorus of boos echoed around St James' Park at the final whistle.

The frustration and anger from the stands came after a 1-0 defeat which included a goalkeeping howler by Lukas Hornicek, a red card for substitute Jacob Ramsey and another blunt attacking performance.
"Big frustration, big disappointment," said Jaissle after a fourth defeat in six Premier League games.

highlights.title: A Concerning Amount of GTA Fans Would Give Up Their Pets to Play GTA 6 Early
highlights.summary: A poll of 1,300 American gamers shows some concerning trends regarding GTA 6 — more specifically, their willingness to abandon their pets for a chance at playing the game ahead of its release. GTA 6 might be the biggest pop culture phenomenon in human history.
body: Before GTA 6’s big debut on Netflix, fans were literally camping outside of Rockstar’s headquarters, using special equipment to monitor oxygen levels, sound volume, and even count cars going in and out of the building for just a sliver of information about the highly-anticipated title.

With just a few more weeks until launch, fans are more amped than ever to play the game — and some would even give up pretty important things if they had the chance to experience it before everyone else.

A new survey by Unwind Media polled 1,347 American gamers to see how they felt about GTA 6. And while there were more than a few surprising responses, one stood out from the rest; according to the survey, 7% of polled fans said they would literally give up their pet for a month if they got to play the game a week early.

Out of these fans, those who already pre-ordered the game were more likely to give up certain things. The number of deadbeat pet parents doubled within this group, with 13% of players who pre-ordered GTA 6 saying they would be willing to give up their pet to play it early.

highlights.title: John Goodman Says Digger Reviews 'Killed' the Movie Before It Was Released
highlights.summary: John Goodman believes the critical reception to Digger "killed" the movie before it had even been released. Tom Cruise's latest film, Digger, is one of the biggest Hollywood bombs of 2026.
body: Cruise's Digger co-star, John Goodman, spoke about the situation with Josh Horowitz and believed that critics pushed anyone away from seeing it. Digger's Rotten Tomatoes score sits at 53%, making it one of Cruise's most divisive movies and the lowest-rated film in his filmography since 2017's The Mummy.

"It hurt. They kinda killed us before we opened [with headlines like], 'This will only make $5," said Goodman. "And it [felt like] a good reason for people to avoid it. I'm proud of it. I had a ball doing it."

Goodman went on to state that he believed in the message of Digger and defended the film, despite it not being universally loved. IGN gave Digger a 6 out of 10, noting that the movie lacks the bite needed to sell its message, but has great performances and humor.

"Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs," reads an excerpt from our review. "If you're an AMC A-List member (or have another cinema subscription), Digger is worth catching on the big screen."

highlights.title: "At Home in Space" opens, caps Air and Space Museum renovation
highlights.summary: After seven years of work and nearly $1 billion, the Smithsonian has completed the renovation of the National Air and Space Museum's flagship building in Washington, DC.
body: On October 30, the museum debuted its last-to-open spaceflight exhibition, returning “home” with a gallery devoted to establishing a spacefaring civilization.

“It’s the prep story, the space shuttle story. It’s what allows us to end up at a place where we have 25-plus years of long-duration spaceflight experience, the capacity for humans to be living in space on the International Space Station (ISS), and then it carries that story forward. So the middle of our story then becomes the ISS, and the end of the story are the next steps,” said Levasseur.

Over the past several years, the National Air and Space Museum has introduced new galleries showcasing how US astronauts first entered space and landed on the Moon (“ Destination Moon ”); how robotic probes have explored every planet in our solar system (“Kenneth C. Griffin Exploring the Planets”); how technologies and infrastructure impact our daily lives (“RTX Living in the Space Age Hall”) and what approaches spaceflight will take in the years to come (“Futures in Space”).

highlights.summary: In an announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its "Grid Protectors Program" at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000…
body: As public opinion has soured on data centers, it’s selling ‘AI campuses’ as protectors, instead of noisy polluters.

The announcement comes as opposition to data centers spreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents. In Utah, residents protested after Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double the state’s peak electricity demand in 2025, and spread hot air in the desert valley surrounding the data center.

Now OpenAI’s approach is to pitch the construction of power plants that feed the electricity required by the new AI data centers it’s building as “a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.”

highlights.title: Johnny Depp Is Open to Playing Jack Sparrow Again in a New Pirates of the Caribbean Movie
highlights.summary: In a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight, Depp was asked if he had any interest in playing Sparrow again. He noted that he wanted to send the franchise off on a better note, presumably referring to the last film being a critical disappointment.
body: Johnny Depp is open to playing Jack Sparrow again in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie, despite saying he'd never work with Disney on the franchise ever again.

"If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they're going to top off the Pirates [story]. The only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note. I'll go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. If it's Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship."

Depp had previously stated during his legal battle with Amber Heard that he wouldn't work with Disney on a new Pirates movie, not even for $300 million and a million alpaca. It seems he's softened his stance on the matter, which has reportedly been the case for a while. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has stated a few times over the last couple of years that he was having conversations with Depp about a new Pirates movie, but nothing has been locked in place. There is, however, a screenplay in the works, and the producer hopes to get a deal signed with Depp.

highlights.title: The Online Right’s Closing Campaign Argument: Fascist Anakin Skywalker Memes
highlights.summary: With Democrats poised to make significant gains in Tuesday’s midterm elections, Trump supporters have been reduced to posting bizarre Star Wars fan fiction.
body: If you quit checking X months ago (or left back when it was still Twitter) and have found yourself wondering how much of a right-wing echo chamber it’s become, just try making sense of the following posts.

Yes, it seems that while the fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) will remain shut down for the foreseeable future, MAGA conservatives are picking up the slack, using the last hours before the 2026 midterms to imagine themselves and Trump-aligned candidates as the disciples of a genocidal archvillain from a space opera.

According to Christian streamer Kangmin Lee, Anakin Skywalker represents the “archetypal disenfranchised chud,” radicalized when he realizes the “political order” he once believed in is “deeply corrupt, hypocritical, and wicked.” Right-wing Substack writer Max Mersault believes that the Anakin posts are “culturally significant” and that you couldn’t “engineer a better anti-progressive memetic virus in [a] lab if you tried.”

highlights.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
highlights.summary: OpenAI is raising Security Bug Bounty rewards and introducing report quality, loyalty, and priority campaign bonuses for independent security researchers.
body: We’re raising rewards in OpenAI’s Security Bug Bounty program to further encourage independent researchers to pursue vulnerabilities in OpenAI software that our testing may have missed. We’re also introducing new incentives for researchers to earn more for higher quality vulnerability reports.

Independent security researchers play an essential role in protecting technology across the industry. At OpenAI, incentivizing responsible disclosure is a core part of our security model, complementing our Defense Factory ⁠ work, where our engineers use our models to find weaknesses, reproduce them, and test fixes.
Today’s updates are designed to encourage and empower researchers, and to continue building a collaborative, community-first security environment.

We’re more than quadrupling the midpoint of our reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings on average. A critical vulnerability in a core product such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will now earn up to $30,000. Exceptional critical findings on those targets remain eligible for up to $100,000, and now up to $172,000 with bonuses. The full details are available in our security bug bounty program ⁠ (opens in a new window).

highlights.title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Co-Showrunner Confirms Harfoots Will Return
highlights.summary: Contrary to earlier reports, the Harfoots are still a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3 albeit not to the degree they were featured in the Prime Video show’s first two seasons.
body: “[We] have not written out the Harfoots [from Season 3]”, co-showrunner Patrick McKay recently informed me at the show’s press junket.

“I would say for myself and J.D. [Payne], my co-show runner, every season is its own opportunity and its own challenge. With Season 3, we really wanted to level up our game as dramatists. We really wanted to focus the show. We wanted to be more psychological, more emotional, wanted to do a darker season,” McKay explained.

“It's the season where Sauron forges the One Ring, and we wanted that to unify every single storyline. We didn't want it to have sprawl the way we enjoyed having in the past. No, no. This was a time we wanted it to be one journey and on rails.”

McKay continued: “That meant that if a story wasn't about the rings and wasn't about Sauron and wasn't about the One Ring, that to put it in there would feel forced and it wouldn't do justice to those characters. But don't worry, you can't count a halfling out, the Harfoots and Markella [Kavenagh] and Megan [Richardson]'s characters. They'll be back maybe sooner than you think.”

highlights.title: ‘Tetsuo’ Director Tsukamoto Shinya on Staying Independent and Why He Can’t Pull Away From War Films
highlights.summary: Beloved independent filmmaker Tsukamoto Shinya gave a masterclass at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival (TIFF), speaking about the pivotal works of his career as well as his most recent film, the English-language feature “Mr.
body: Tsukamoto recalled shooting the film on 16mm, before the era of digital VFX.

“No CG. We had a little bit of tokusatsu [practical special effects] technology at the time but this didn’t use any of that, this used stuff which was thrown out on the street and we basically stuck it on [Taguchi Tomorowo]’s face,” the director said. Of the effect of Taguchi gliding through the streets, he said to “think of it as really rough stop motion.”

The film took about a year to make, Tsukamoto said, though “the time we spent with the crew was shorter, a lot of the time towards the end I was working alone – like the sparks flying off at the end [of the clip], that was something I worked on alone.”
The success of “Tetsuo,” he said, took him to film festivals overseas and led to his second feature, the horror film “Hiruko the Goblin,” now with a higher budget.

highlights.title: Sweaty, triumphant and decked out in neon: I asked NYC Marathon runners what they wore – in pictures
highlights.summary: On 1 November, 61,000 people ran in the 2026 New York City Marathon. We asked about the running gear – and motivations – that carried them to the finish line. The best women’s running shoes for roads and trails.
body: The sea of orange thermal blankets, shiny medals and brightly colored running shoes is impossible to miss.
On 1 November, 61,000 people took over New York City’s streets for the 2026 NYC Marathon. Making it through the 26.2-mile race is a feat that takes grit, endurance and … the right gear.

Near Central Park, blocks from the finish line, I navigated swarms of proud parents and groups holding neon posters emblazoned “hot girls run marathons”, asking runners about their sneakers, energy fuel and shorts. (It turns out Nike Alphaflys are a marathon favorite.) When I couldn’t find exact matches for their items, I linked to brands with similar options.

From a 71-year-old who has run the NYC Marathon over 30 times to an Olympic trial qualifier who placed seventh in her age group – marathoners also shared what brought them to the starting line, with stories that remind us there is more than one way to be a runner, and just as many reasons to keep showing up.

highlights.title: Apple is ‘not able to predict’ when it’ll have enough iPhone Duos to go around
highlights.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus doesn't have a timeline for when iPhone Duo supply constraints could lift. During an interview with Reuters, Ternus said the company is "working hard to get it to as many customers as quickly as possible, but at this ​point, we're not able to predict when supply and demand…
body: Apple launched its first foldable last month for $1,999, featuring a 5.4 outer display and 7.6-inch inner screen. Preorders for the iPhone Duo quickly sold out, with some shipments expected to arrive in 2027. Apple also made a limited number of iPhone Duo models available in-store at launch.
In his interview with Reuters, Ternus also addressed reports about cracked screens, saying “a very small percentage” of iPhone Duos were returned for this issue, and that Apple is replacing them.

The company has contended with supply chain constraints and rising memory costs for months now. This resulted in price increases across its product lineup, along with higher iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starting prices. “What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” Ternus said during Apple’s Q4 2026 earnings call on Monday. Ternus added that the company expects to see “even higher memory costs” during Apple’s December quarter but notes that this is “partly offset” by recent price increases.
Even without a standard iPhone 18 model, Apple reported record-breaking iPhone revenue at $57.58 billion during its fourth quarter.

highlights.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
highlights.summary: OpenAI is preparing its next internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and strengthen its defenses using AI.
body: We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI, bringing new researchers and security partners together with our own teams to use our models to test and strengthen our systems. We’re partnering with Cathedral, whose researchers will use OpenAI’s models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses, bringing differentiated expertise and approaches to finding weaknesses and helping us protect our platforms.

We’re also making improvements to our Security Bug Bounty program including more than quadrupling our rewards for critical findings. We want researchers to challenge our assumptions and help strengthen both our systems and the methods we use to defend them.

This is part of our ongoing effort to use AI to continuously find and fix weaknesses in our systems. Our last sprint showed what this approach can deliver. We dedicated 25% of our product engineers to finding and fixing weaknesses in our systems. Using Codex, engineers investigated findings, reproduced vulnerabilities in isolated environments and prepared patches for review.

highlights.title: Carragher: Boring Newcastle face a tough season ahead
highlights.summary: Jamie Carragher described Newcastle as flat and boring following their defeat to Everton on Monday Night Football and reckons Matthias Jaissle's side faces a difficult season.
body: Thierno Barry's second-half goal earned Everton a 1-0 win at St James' Park and their first away victory in the Premier League this season, as Newcastle were booed off at half-time and full-time following their fourth defeat in five games across all competitions.
Newcastle have slipped to 13th and are now four points above the bottom three, with a trip to lowly Fulham to come on Saturday.

"I think it is going to be a tough season for them," said Sky Sports' Carragher. "I felt tonight [Monday] was actually more important for Newcastle than the cup game [Carabao Cup loss at Everton last week], and it was the other way round for Everton, who are desperate for a trophy.
"But I fear a little bit for Newcastle, I think it could be a long, tough season."

highlights.title: World of Warcraft Forever release time in your time zone
highlights.summary: The release of World of Warcraft: Forever brings a third — or, depending on how you count them, a sixth or seventh — way to play World of Warcraft to everyone with a WoW subscription.
body: You'll be able to delve into WoW as it felt like 22 years ago, but never actually was, this week on Nov. 4 (or Nov. 5, depending on your time zone). Here's when World of Warcraft: Forever releases in your time zone.
WoW: Forever is a kind of retro remix of WoW, based on the content and design philosophy of the classic game but with some new stuff, some modernizations, and some changes.

The core of Forever is the original nine character classes and eight playable races, split into two warring factions who can never communicate with each other or group up together: The Horde and Alliance. All the adventuring zones, dungeons, raids, and cities of the original game are present across its two massive continents.
Access to WoW: Forever is included in a World of Warcraft subscription, but the Skyborne (and access to their starting zone) are sold separately.

highlights.title: A Royal Surprise: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu
highlights.summary: The wildly anticipated Korean fantasy romance, starring Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young, will launch with four episodes Nov. 3, followed by two new installments every Wednesday.
body: In a surprise gift to fans, Disney + and Hulu are moving up the royal arrival of The Remarried Empress, bringing the lavish Korean fantasy romance to viewers Nov. 3, one day ahead of its previously announced premiere.

Stars Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young revealed the change Tuesday at a press conference in Seoul. The first four episodes will be available at launch, with Disney describing the early release as a thank you to fans for their support.

Based on the hit Naver Webtoon, The Remarried Empress combines palace intrigue, romantic betrayal and an impossibly elegant heroine determined to claim her own future. Shin plays Navier, the empress of the Eastern Empire, whose marriage unravels when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu (Ju), falls for escaped slave girl Rashta (Lee Se-young). Navier agrees to his request for a divorce on one condition: She must be permitted to marry her own budding love — Crown Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) of the rival Western Kingdom.
The series was adapted for the screen by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol and directed by Cho Suwon, whose credits include Still 17 and Pinocchio.
